Investigating — current findings so far:
- Autoscaler did an aggressive ramp on a subset of k8s pools this morning (06:50–07:10 ET) due to an unrelated batch job mislabeling. Some workers were evicted and re-created; during the window we saw a transient increase in tokenization latency and a small number of OOM restarts.
- I’m seeing error traces consistent with HTTP 502/504 from the fronting NGINX layer when instances were mid-restart. Not yet seeing model-level CUDA OOMs.
- There is a hot prefix in the Blue Harbor workload causing KV-cache thrash when nodes move; this amplifies tail latency.

Immediate mitigations in progress:
1) Pinning a hot subset of instances (no rolling restarts) for Blue Harbor traffic only.
2) Enabling prefix-aware KV cache hold for the affected shards.
3) Throttle inbound per-tenant concurrent requests at the edge for 30m to break retry loops.

I’ll push a debug bundle (redwood-debug-log-20261114.txt) to the ticket and follow up in 20–30 minutes.

— Marissa (SRE)

Added technical detail from routing: we saw a sudden increase in request fan-out to model-variants due to a misconfiguration in a routing policy rollout stage; fallback-to-variant logic caused simultaneous model loads which contributed to memory pressure on a small subset of hosts.

Actions taken:
- Temporarily disabled the rollout policy that increased fan-out.
- Marked 4 hosts as quarantined for live investigation.
- Enabled lower-cost quantized variant as immediate fallback for new sessions.

Expect decreased 5xx within ~15–25 minutes if no other downstream cascades occur.

— Sean (Infra)

Julia — quick update and the steps we recommend while we stabilize (ETA for primary mitigation: 20–30 minutes):

What we saw: brief autoscaler-triggered restarts + routing fan-out that together produced transient memory pressure and fronting 502/504s. Secondary effect: your client retries amplified the failure window.

What we are doing (engineer actions):
- Pinning Blue Harbor traffic to a hot pool and preventing rolling restarts for affected nodes.
- Applying a prefix-aware KV cache hold to reduce cache thrash.
- Disabling the rollout stage that increased model fan-out; enabling quantized fallback variant for new sessions.
- Throttling per-tenant concurrent clients briefly at the edge for 30 minutes to break retry amplification.

Customer checklist (quick actions you can apply now):
- Reduce client concurrency from 50 -> 20 per host and add exponential backoff with jitter.
- Failover to the quantized variant endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/models/thunderbolt-quantized (stateless, slightly lower quality)
- If you have a queued ingestion pipeline, stagger retries with a randomized 500–1000ms jitter window.

ETA and next update: primary mitigations should take effect in ~20–30 minutes (by ~10:15 ET). I’ll post a follow-up once we confirm error rates are back to normal and share the debug bundle.
